preconditions.description: The number of cities n is an integer between 2 and 200,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: len(roads) == n - 1 and all(1 <= s <= n and 1 <= t <= n and s != t for s, t in roads)
preconditions.description: There are exactly n-1 roads, each connecting two distinct cities with valid indices (1 to n).

preconditions.expression: all(connected(s, t) or connected(t, s) for s in range(1, n + 1) for t in range(s + 1, n + 1))
preconditions.description: The undirected graph formed by the roads is connected (ignoring road directions). Here, connected(s, t) means there exists a path from s to t in the undirected graph.

postconditions.description: The first line of stdout is the minimum number of roads to flip (min_flips) to make all roads point away from the chosen capital(s). The second line is a space-separated list of all possible capital choices, sorted in increasing order.

postconditions.expression: min_flips == min(sum(1 for s, t in roads if t == s) for s in range(1, n + 1))
postconditions.description: min_flips is the smallest number of roads that need to be flipped so that, for the chosen capital(s), all roads point away from the capital (i.e., for every road (s, t), if s is the capital, t must be the destination, and vice versa).

postconditions.expression: all(capital in capitals for capital in range(1, n + 1) if sum(1 for s, t in roads if (s == capital and t != capital) or (t == capital and s != capital)) == min_flips)
postconditions.description: Every city listed in capitals is a valid capital choice that achieves the minimum number of flips (min_flips).
